title: Public-Sector Contact Center Advisor
summary: An internal web service that helps public-sector contact-center agents follow live STT transcription during a call, then review AI analysis and consultation history after it ends. I designed and implemented the frontend across agent and manager workflows.

projectIntro.title: Project overview
projectIntro.description: Live transcription and connection status matter during a call, while durable consultation history and AI analysis matter after it ends. I designed the screens and state flow so agents retain the same context as call state changes.

service.label: Service
service.description: An internal web service supporting public-sector contact-center work

users.label: Users
users.description: Agents handling live calls and managers reviewing consultation status and history

role.label: My scope
role.description: Designed and implemented agent and manager UI, live transcription, call state, connection recovery, and consultation history

problem.title: Problem and requirements
problem.description: Live call data and durable post-call data arrive at different times, but the consultation context had to remain one continuous screen flow.

liveContext.title: Preserve live consultation context
liveContext.description: Agents needed to detect active calls quickly and follow speaker-specific STT transcription and current connection state without delay during a call.

afterCall.title: Continue work after the call
afterCall.description: After a call ended, agents needed to review AI analysis and durable consultation history in the context of the same consultation.

roleScope.title: Role-appropriate screens
roleScope.description: Agents and managers use the same call information but require different scopes across live consultation, monitoring, history, and settings.

design.title: Frontend design
design.description: I modeled call-state and transcription-event transitions before individual screens, then built role-specific UI and data responsibilities on that state model.

callState.title: Call-state model
callState.description: I modeled the current call as idle, live, or ended so new-call detection, live transcription, and post-call history transition according to explicit state.

streamState.title: Transcription-event model
streamState.description: Snapshot, partial and final speech, call completion, and analysis completion or failure become reducer events that translate differently timed data into consistent UI state.

roleUi.title: Role-specific UI composition
roleUi.description: Protected routes and role-specific layout regions separate agent and manager screens. TanStack Query owns server data, while Zustand owns the current call and selection state.

decisions.title: Technical decisions
decisions.description: To balance real-time behavior with recoverability, I switched data paths by call state and managed stream events and connection state explicitly.

transport.title: Switch between polling and SSE
transport.description: Polling runs only while finding a new call, while call-scoped SSE owns the latest state during a call. Polling resumes after the call ends to find the next call.

reducer.title: Separate partial and final speech
reducer.description: Partial speech uses speaker-specific temporary regions. Final speech is deduplicated by conversation identifier and sorted by start time so the UI does not depend on stream arrival order.

recovery.title: Recover without losing context
recovery.description: Heartbeat monitoring, staged retries, and manual reconnection preserve finalized transcription until a new snapshot reconciles current state.

contributions.title: Core implementation
contributions.description: I implemented the agent-facing frontend flow from live consultation through post-call analysis and history, along with role-specific management screens.

consultation.title: Live consultation screen
consultation.description: I connected active-call detection, speaker-specific STT transcription, call and connection state, and post-call AI analysis into one consultation flow.

history.title: Consultation history navigation
history.description: I implemented consultation history and added search, favorites, and a favorites-only tab in response to agent feedback.

roles.title: Agent and manager screens
roles.description: Side panels, tabs, and main panels compose by role, with loading states and error boundaries applied at the panel level.

resilience.title: Connection and recovery experience
resilience.description: Retry state and recovery points remain visible so agents keep previously confirmed transcription and continue into next-call detection after a disconnect.

verification.title: Core scenarios I verified
verification.description: I evaluated the live interface not only under a healthy connection, but also by whether it preserves consultation context across event-order and reconnection scenarios.

stateTransition.title: Call-state transitions
stateTransition.description: I checked the idle, live, and ended transitions to confirm that polling and SSE start and stop in the correct state.

eventConsistency.title: Transcription-event consistency
eventConsistency.description: I checked that partial speech stays in speaker-specific temporary regions and finalized speech remains deduplicated and ordered by start time.

recovery.title: Recovery without context loss
recovery.description: I checked that finalized transcription survives staged retries and manual reconnection, then reconciles with a fresh snapshot.

flow.title: I switched between live and durable data paths through call state.
flow.description: While idle, the frontend looks for an active call. Once a call begins, reducer-managed SSE events drive the UI. After the call ends, the live connection closes and the flow continues into AI analysis and consultation history.
flow.alt: Frontend state flow from active-call detection through call state, SSE, transcription reducer, and consultation UI
flow.caption: SSE owns live state during a call; next-call detection and durable history continue after it ends.
